description: baseline

Build the first real recipe in submissions/arena/: an airbench96-style net without TTA. Settings: frozen patch-whitening conv (2x2, fit in prepare on real train images), dirac init, widths 128/384/576, depth 3 per block, BatchNorm-bias lr x64, Nesterov SGD lr 9 / wd 0.012 / bs 1024, label smoothing 0.3, lookahead, alternating flip plus translate-2 on GPU. The whole train set lives on the GPU as uint8 and is loaded in prepare. Use channels_last with bf16/fp16 autocast. torch.compile and warmup run in build() on synthetic data, covering the full batch, the final partial batch and eval shapes. Train for 10 epochs. Eval is a plain forward with no TTA and must handle any B from 1 to 1024.

Third point of the epoch sweep on the base recipe: 9 epochs, or 11 if the 10-epoch run missed 0.753. Fit accuracy against epochs with the 8.5 and 10 points and find the knee at 0.753 to within 0.5 epochs.
rerun E002 unchanged (noise floor)
Base recipe at its knee epoch count, with label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3. Nothing else changes.

Built on the first feasible airbench96-style base (I001/I003 knee). Make one systems change and leave the recipe alone. Move the whole training step into one torch.compile'd function: forward, backward, Nesterov SGD update and lookahead blend. Apply the update with torch._foreach_* ops (or SGD foreach/fused=True) so there is no per-parameter Python loop. Pass lr and the lookahead schedule as 0-d GPU tensors so changing them never triggers a recompile. Compile and warm up this function in build() on synthetic data, covering the full batch and the final partial batch. Keep the epoch count, seeds, lr, wd, LS and widths identical to the base.

Change one thing in the E002 recipe: the epoch count, from 9 to 8.5. Scale the lr/lookahead schedule to the new total step count, so the shape stays the same over fewer steps. The last half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation. The final partial batch is still the shape that was compiled in build(). Everything else stays bit-identical to E002 (commit 479b9a3).

Target conv throughput: cuDNN conv kernels are about 75% of GPU time but run at only about 30% of bf16 peak. On the E002 recipe at 9 epochs, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True before warmup in build() and compile the model step with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', so Inductor benchmarks its Triton conv/GEMM templates against cuDNN for every shape (full batch, partial batch, eval) on synthetic inputs. All autotuning stays in untimed build(). If the base already has one of these settings, add only the missing one.
Base recipe at its knee epoch count with lookahead removed: plain Nesterov SGD, no weight averaging. Same lr, wd and schedule.

One systems change on the tip recipe (E007 commit 52204ad: 9 epochs, LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark plus max-autotune-no-cudagraphs). Replace the final global adaptive_max_pool2d (and any other adaptive pool in the net) with an equivalent reduction, x.amax(dim=(2,3)), or F.max_pool2d with a fixed kernel equal to the spatial size. Its backward then becomes a dense masked/eq kernel that Inductor can fuse, instead of the atomic scatter kernel that took 0.48 ms/step (~2.5% of GPU time) in the E003 profile. The forward math is identical. Recompile and warm up in build() for the full batch, the partial batch and eval shapes. Nothing else changes.

One systems change on the tip recipe (E007 commit 52204ad: 9 epochs, LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark plus max-autotune-no-cudagraphs). Replace the final global adaptive_max_pool2d (and any other adaptive pool in the net) with an equivalent reduction, x.amax(dim=(2,3)), or F.max_pool2d with a fixed kernel equal to the spatial size. Its backward then becomes a dense masked/eq kernel that Inductor can fuse, instead of the atomic scatter kernel that took 0.48 ms/step (~2.5% of GPU time) in the E003 profile. The forward math is identical. Recompile and warm up in build() for the full batch, the partial batch and eval shapes. Nothing else changes.

Test the width claim in the direction that saves time. On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), shrink the last block from 576 to 512 channels and keep everything else, head input included, consistent. Block 3 is roughly a third of the network's FLOPs (conv1 at 8x8 plus two convs at 4x4), so this cuts about 5-6% of FLOPs. Record per-epoch time and per-seed accuracy.

Schedule shape (D001 flagged that the tree has no node for it). On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), change only the lr schedule's warmup: halve the warmup fraction (for example from ~23% of steps to ~12%), keep the same peak lr 9, and decay linearly to exactly zero at the final step. If the base already decays to zero, change only the warmup fraction. The lookahead schedule stays tied to step count as before.
Explore: on the feasible base, run the first ~35% of epochs on 24 px random crops and the rest at full 32 px. Compile both resolutions in build(). Same epoch count as the knee.

Corrected version of I007 that changes only one thing. On the E002 recipe (bs 1024, 9 epochs, same schedule shape), optimize the 4D conv filters (all except the frozen whitening conv) with Muon: Nesterov momentum 0.6, lr about 0.24, 5 Newton-Schulz quintic steps in bf16, with the update scaled by sqrt(max(1, out/in)) on the flattened [out, in*k*k] matrix. BatchNorm biases and the head stay on the existing Nesterov SGD with the same lr/wd. Keep lookahead. Compile the NS loop in build(). Log the optimizer step time separately.

Explore where capacity sits. On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), cut the first block's depth from 3 convs to 2: drop one 128->128 3x3 conv at 16x16 and leave blocks 2 and 3 at depth 3. This removes about 6% of the FLOPs, the cheapest-per-accuracy capacity if H1.5 is right that the late layers matter most for a 100-way head. Dirac init, widths and everything else stay unchanged.

Exploit E014. Port the E014 Muon optimizer exactly as it was onto the tip E010 commit (5aa9aa5: LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark, max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, F.max_pool2d head). Muon settings: conv filters except the frozen whitening conv, Nesterov momentum 0.6, lr 0.24, 5 quintic NS steps in bf16, update scaled by sqrt(max(1,out/in)) on the flattened [out,in*k*k] matrix. BN biases and the head stay on the existing SGD, and lookahead is kept. Make ONE recipe change: epochs 9 -> 8, with the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules scaled to the new step count. The final partial batch shape is compiled in build(). Before launching, run the one-step finite-gradient check (drafts/debug_nan.py), because the compiled NS and Muon graph is new to the tip's compile mode. Log the optimizer step time separately.

Cut Muon's per-step overhead. E014 added ~10% time, or ~1.9 ms/step, for NS. Take the Muon 8-epoch recipe above and change only the Newton-Schulz iteration count from 5 to 3 quintic steps, keeping the same coefficients (airbench94_muon uses 3; D002 C0013-C0015 show final quality is insensitive to exact orthogonalization). Keep everything else identical. Report the optimizer step time per step against the 5-step run.

Find the Muon knee below 8 epochs. Run this after the Muon 8-epoch run, and only if it scores >=0.758. Take the better of the 5-step and 3-step NS variants and change only the epoch count, from 8 to 7.5. Scale all schedules to the step count. The last half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation, as in E006.

Tune Muon's lr, which was inherited untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe (or 7.5 epochs if that becomes the tip), change only the Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.36. The SGD lr for BN biases and the head stays the same. If it falls by more than 0.25 pp, the follow-up direction is 0.16.

Test whether Muon's update normalization replaces averaging. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe, remove lookahead (plain Muon + Nesterov SGD, no weight averaging) and change nothing else. Compare it paired against the Muon 8-epoch run with lookahead. This is purely informative about the H4.2/H1.2 interaction: it decides whether averaging tuning (H1.6) is still worth runs on the Muon base.

Systems change that transfers to any recipe. On the current tip (the Muon successor if one is kept, else E010), replace GELU with SiLU everywhere and change nothing else. SiLU's sigmoid is cheaper than GELU's erf, and Inductor may fuse its BN+act backward with less recompute. Run the one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first (E009 lesson), and re-profile the Triton elementwise share.

Find the Muon knee below 7.5 epochs. On the tip E018 (commit d634e3b: Muon NS3, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead, LS 0.2, 7.5 epochs), change only the epoch count from 7.5 to 7.0. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. 7 epochs is a whole number, so the half-epoch permutation trick is not needed. The final partial batch shape stays the one compiled in build(). Nothing else changes.

Systems change to the Muon optimizer step only; the recipe math stays the same. Muon currently costs 1.93 ms/step of GPU time (about 10% of the step), mostly as many small kernels: 9 per-param calls, each with momentum, norm and projection ops plus per-iteration NS elementwise work. Replace them with one torch.compile'd Muon step over all conv filters. Do the momentum and Nesterov update with torch._foreach_* ops. Stack same-shape flattened filters within each block (128x1152, 384x3456, 576x5184 pairs) and run the 3 quintic NS iterations as one bmm per shape group. Apply the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling and the weight-norm projection inside the same compiled function. Pass the Muon lr as a 0-d GPU tensor so schedule changes do not recompile. Compile and warm up in build() on synthetic tensors. Run the drafts/debug_nan.py one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching (E009 lesson). Measure the Muon step GPU time with drafts/time_muon.py before and after.

Pre-registered follow-up to E019 (Muon lr 0.36 cost 1.04 pp on every seed). On the current tip (the 7.0-epoch Muon run if it is kept, else E018 at 7.5 epochs), change only the Muon lr for the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.16. The SGD lr for BN biases, whitening bias and head, the schedule shape, lookahead and NS3 all stay unchanged.

Lower the end-of-schedule floor for the Muon group only. E019's post-mortem says the Muon lr is an unbuffered per-step relative rotation, and the 0.07x terminal floor leaves end-of-training noise that lookahead cannot average out. On the current tip, change only the Muon group's lr multiplier so it decays linearly to 0 at the final step instead of to 0.07x. The warmup and the rest of the decay keep the same shape. The SGD group (BN biases, head) keeps its existing schedule, including its 0.07x floor. Lookahead is unchanged.

Explore Muon momentum, inherited untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon at bs ~2000. On the current tip, change only the Muon Nesterov momentum from 0.6 to 0.8. Muon lr, NS3, lookahead and the SGD group stay the same. Rationale: at bs 1024 with a 100-way head, per-step gradients are noisier than in the bs-2000 CIFAR-10 setting. Heavier momentum averages more before orthogonalization, which normalizes away gradient magnitude, so momentum is the only knob that filters direction noise.

Trim the Muon knee by a quarter epoch. On the current tip (E023 commit 9c08ac0: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead, LS 0.2, SiLU, 7.0 epochs; or the I027/I028 successor if either is kept), change only the epoch count from 7.0 to 6.75. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. The last quarter-epoch uses the first quarter of that epoch's permutation, as in E006/E018. The final partial batch must be a shape compiled in build(); add it to the warmup if it is new. Nothing else changes. If I027 or I028 is kept with a gain of 0.2 pp or more, use 6.5 epochs instead (one epoch-count change from that tip).

Lengthen the lookahead averaging window on the Muon base. E020 shows averaging is worth ~0.9 pp with Muon, and the schedule (decay 0.95^5 x (t/T)^3, sync every 5 steps) was inherited untuned from CIFAR-10. On the current tip, change only the lookahead base decay from 0.95^5 (~0.774 per sync) to 0.97^5 (~0.859 per sync). That roughly doubles the effective averaging horizon late in training. The (t/T)^3 ramp, the sync interval of 5 steps, the final-weights handling and everything else stay unchanged.

Combine the E011 near-miss with the epoch exchange rate. E011 priced block-3 width at ~0.13 pp per 1% of time, while cutting Muon epochs costs only ~0.056 pp per 1% (E022: 0.38 pp for 6.8%). So extra block-3 width paid for by fewer epochs should be a net win. On the current tip, widen only block 3 from 576 to 640 channels (a multiple of 64 for tensor-core tiling), keeping the head input and Muon groups consistent; the 640-wide filters stay batched as a same-shape pair in the compiled NS. Epochs stay at the tip's count. Run the one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first, and warm up the new shapes in build().

Explore the D003 mechanism (C0016/C0017): how a 4D kernel is split before orthogonalization. Replace the flattened [out, in*9] orthogonalization with a real frequency-wise variant of Muon-C. Project each 3x3 kernel momentum onto an orthonormal real 3x3 basis (the tensor product of the 3-point orthonormal DCT-II), which gives 9 [out, in] matrices per layer. Orthogonalize them with one batched 3-step NS (bmm over the 9 frequencies), then transform back to the spatial domain. The output scaling uses sqrt(max(1,out/in)) on the [out,in] shape. Keep the weight-norm projection, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead and the epoch count of the current tip. Compile in build() and run the one-step finite-gradient check first.

Muon's updates have a fixed magnitude (an orthogonalized step against a weight-norm projection), so the SGD-style warmup (23% of steps ramping from 0.2x) may waste early steps for the conv filters. On the current tip, change only the Muon group's lr multiplier during warmup: hold it at 1.0x from step 0, and keep the existing decay shape and floor after the warmup point. The SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) keeps its full warmup schedule. Lookahead, NS3, momentum and epochs are unchanged. Check finite gradients for the first ~20 steps on synthetic data in drafts/ before launching.

Systems change to the conv shapes, with the learning recipe unchanged. First, in drafts/, print the activation spatial sizes per block and run a per-layer profile of the tip (untimed, not an experiment). If the unpadded 2x2 whitening conv outputs 31x31, block 1's first conv runs at 31x31, and max-pool(2) then floors that to 15x15, so its last row and column are computed and discarded. Make one change: slice the whitening output to [..., :30, :30] in the model's forward, identically in train and eval. This is a fixed architecture step, not TTA, and eval still accepts 32x32 inputs for any B. Every downstream pooled shape is unchanged (15/7/3); the only math change is that row and column 29 see zero padding instead of row and column 30. Warm up the new shapes in build() and run the finite-gradient check. If the profile shows the net already runs at even sizes (32/16/8/4), skip this idea and mark H2.5.2 not applicable.

On the current tip (E028 commit e95ff94: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, 6.5 epochs), make one change: the Muon group's terminal lr floor goes from 0.07x to 0.15x. Shift the linear decay after warmup so it ends at 0.15x at the final step. Warmup shape, peak, the SGD group's schedule (floor stays 0.07x), lookahead, epochs and everything else stay unchanged. This is the untested direction opposite E025, where decay-to-0 cost 0.51 pp on the Muon group.

Systems change; the recipe is unchanged during the first epoch. On the tip, train the whitening-conv bias only for the first epoch (~49 of ~319 steps), as airbench94_muon/Hiverge do. After that, call a second compiled train-step variant where whiten.bias is detached / requires_grad=False. The whitening output then needs no grad, and the backward skips the input-gradient (dgrad) of block 1's first 24->128 conv at 31x31 plus the whitening-bias reduction. Compile and warm up BOTH variants in build() on synthetic data (full and partial batch) so the switch never recompiles in the timed region. Lookahead still blends the frozen bias (a no-op once it is fixed). Run drafts/debug_nan.py on both graphs under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first.

On the tip, after training ends and the final lookahead-averaged weights are in place (inside train(), so it is timed), recompute the BN running statistics. Reset running_mean/var, set BN momentum=None (cumulative average), and run a no-grad train-mode forward over 12 batches of 1024 training images: un-augmented, normalized as in training, bf16 autocast, channels_last. Restore the momentum afterwards. Compile and warm up this train-mode no-grad forward in build() on synthetic data. Before launching, check in drafts/ whether lookahead currently blends BN buffers; recalibration replaces them either way. The learning recipe is otherwise unchanged.

On the tip at 6.5 epochs, change only the label smoothing, from 0.2 to 0.1. E004 tested LS only between 0.2 and 0.3, and only on SGD at 9 epochs. Hiverge uses 0.09 at ~7.65 epochs. Everything else (Muon, SGD group, lookahead, augmentation, epochs) stays identical.

Test whether reallocating FLOPs from block-1 depth to epochs pays now that the Muon epoch slope is steep (1.14 pp/epoch for 7.5% time between 6.5 and 7). On the tip, cut block 1 from 3 convs to 2 (drop one 128->128 3x3 conv) and raise epochs from 6.5 to 7.0, with all schedules scaled to the new step count. These are the two halves of one time-matched reallocation. The Muon NS group for 128x1152 now has one matrix instead of a pair; warm up the new shapes, including the 7-epoch final partial batch, in build(), and run the finite-gradient check.

Systems change, math unchanged. Gate it first in drafts/: compare the batched Muon step's wall span (cuda events around it) with the sum of its kernel times from the profiler. Launch only if the gap is 0.4 ms/step or more. If so, capture the compiled Muon step (foreach Nesterov momentum, NS3 bmm per shape group, sqrt(out/in) scaling, weight-norm projection) in a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph during build() on synthetic tensors. Use static .grad buffers (zero_grad(set_to_none=False)), a 0-d lr tensor updated with fill_, and parameters and momentum buffers that prepare() resets IN PLACE (copy_/zero_), so the captured addresses stay valid across trials. Replay the graph each step. Everything else stays unchanged.

On the tip (E028 commit e95ff94: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, 6.5 epochs; or I037's successor if it is kept), make one change: halve the head (final linear layer) lr in the SGD group. If the code expresses the head lr as a multiple of the group's base lr, halve that multiple; otherwise halve the head param-group lr. Keep lr*wd constant for the head, which means doubling its wd so the decay per step is unchanged. BN-bias lr x64, the whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, augmentation and epochs all stay identical. Background: the head lr was inherited from CIFAR-10 SGD airbench (lr 9). That setting faced 10 outputs over ~10 epochs. Here the 100-way head trains against Muon-normalized features over 6.5 epochs, so the head may be overshooting. This is a pure hyperparameter change, so no new compiled shapes are needed. If the lr is passed as a 0-d tensor, nothing recompiles.

Reallocate time from full-res epochs to cheap low-res epochs. The Muon epoch slope at the knee is now steep (~1.14 pp/epoch, ~0.15 pp per 1% time). E013 priced 24 px epochs at only ~0.058 pp per 1% on SGD, so low-res epochs should now be cheaper than full-res ones. On the tip (E034 commit f74c715: Muon NS3 batched, lr 0.16, mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, ~6.5 epochs), make one curriculum change. Train the first 1.5 epochs on whole images bilinearly downsampled to 24 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment, after flip/translate). Then train 5.25 epochs at 32 px, for 6.75 epochs total. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count; bs stays 1024. The frozen whitening conv is reused unchanged. In drafts/, first print the per-block spatial sizes at 24 px input. Set the final pool for each resolution graph to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to that graph's final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (the E009 Inductor bug). Compile and warm up every variant in build() on synthetic data: 24 px with whitening-bias grad, 24 px without it, 32 px without it, plus each full and partial batch shape. Eval stays the 32 px graph. Run drafts/debug_nan.py on every graph under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching.

On the tip, raise the batch size from 1024 to 1536 at 6.5 epochs (~212 steps instead of ~319), with all schedules scaled to the step count. The Muon lr stays at 0.16 (normalized updates). Scale the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) as batch size requires: if the code already uses airbench's per-example lr normalization (lr/bs), keep the configured values; otherwise scale the SGD lr x1.5 and keep lr*wd constant. Lookahead syncs every 5 steps as before. Warm up the new full and partial batch shapes in build().

On the tip, add per-image brightness and contrast jitter inside the compiled GPU augment, applied to the [0,1]-scaled images before normalization and whitening: x = (x - mean_img) * (1 + U(-1,1)*0.13) + mean_img + U(-1,1)*0.14, drawn independently per sample, with alternating flip and translate-2 kept. The RNG comes from the trial-seeded generator in prepare. Eval is unchanged. Warm up the new augment graph in build() on synthetic data.

Move the resolution boundary later on the E040 tip (commit 18ce8ac: Muon NS3 batched, lr 0.16, mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for 1.5 epochs then 32 px for 5.25, 6.75 epochs total). Make one change: train at 24 px for the first 2.25 epochs and at 32 px for the last 4.5, keeping 6.75 epochs total, bs 1024 and the same step-indexed lr, Muon and lookahead schedules, which do not change because the total step count is unchanged. If the switch now falls mid-epoch, take the first part of that epoch's permutation at 24 px and the rest at 32 px, so the sample stream is unchanged. The whitening-bias freeze stays at the end of epoch 1. Before launching, check that every shape used in the timed path is warmed up in build(): 24 px with and without whitening-bias grad, 32 px without it, and any new partial-batch shape at the switch. Warm up with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Run debug_nan.py on any new graph, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times. Risk to note: E040's 1.5 low-res epochs covered roughly the warmup phase (~23% of steps). This change pushes low-res into the peak-lr phase, where full-res steps may matter more.

Add a middle 28 px stage to the E040 curriculum. On the E040 tip, make one change: 24 px for epochs 0-1.5 as now, then whole images bilinearly downsampled (antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip/translate) to 28 px for 1.5 epochs, then 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs. Total stays 6.75 epochs, bs 1024, step-indexed schedules unchanged. In drafts/, print the per-block spatial sizes at 28 px input first (expect whitening 27 -> pools 13/6/3). Set the 28 px graph's final pool to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to its final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (the E009 Inductor bug). Compile and warm up the 28 px train step without whitening-bias grad, plus any partial batch at the stage switches, in build() with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times to catch warmup gaps. Eval stays the 32 px graph.

On the E040 tip, double the head (final linear layer) lr in the SGD group. Keep lr*wd constant for the head by halving its wd. If the code expresses the head lr as a multiple of the group base lr, double that multiple; otherwise double the head param-group lr. The BN-bias lr x64, whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, the resolution curriculum and the epochs stay identical. This is a pure hyperparameter change: the lr is passed as a 0-d tensor, so there are no new shapes and nothing recompiles. Pre-registered follow-up to E039, where halving the head lr cost 0.41 pp on the then-tip.

Win back the bs-1536 accuracy loss through the Muon lr. This is the follow-up pre-registered in I042. At bs 1536 the run takes about 1/3 fewer fixed-magnitude, weight-norm-projected Muon rotations (~212 instead of ~319 steps), so the total rotation path of each filter shrank by about 33%. On the tip (the curriculum-stacked commit if the idea above is kept, else E042), change only the Muon lr for the conv filters, from 0.16 to 0.20. Momentum 0.8, NS3, projection, the schedule shape and floor, the SGD group, lookahead, augmentation and epochs all stay identical. The lr is a 0-d tensor, so nothing recompiles.

Make the warmup-phase resolution stage cheaper. On the current tip (E042 commit 2b85e5e: bs 1536, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for the first 1.5 epochs then 32 px, 6.75 epochs total, SGD-group lr x1.5, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only; or I052's successor if it is kept, in which case change only its first stage), make one change: the first stage's resolution goes from 24 px to 20 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip/translate/jitter). The stage boundary (1.5 epochs), total epochs, bs and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged, so the sample stream and lr values are identical. Rationale: E040 vs E043 show low-res steps are roughly free during the warmup phase but cost accuracy after it, so the cheapest lever left in that phase is to make its steps cheaper rather than more numerous. In drafts/, first print the per-block spatial sizes at 20 px input (expected: whitening 19, block1 19 -> pool 9, block2 9 -> pool 4, block3 4 -> pool 2, final map 2x2) and set the 20 px graph's final pool to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to that final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (E009 Inductor bug). In build(), warm up the 20 px train step with and without whitening-bias grad at bs 1536, plus every partial-batch shape at the 1.5-epoch switch, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Run debug_nan.py on the new graphs under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and compare trial-0 vs later-trial train times. Eval stays the 32 px graph.

Stack E044's 28 px middle stage onto the E045 tip. This combines a near-miss with a margin that can absorb it. The tip is E045 (commit bfcff33): bs 1536, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5 then 32 px, 6.75 epochs total, SGD-group lr x1.5, head lr x2 with wd halved, Muon lr 0.16 mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, brightness/contrast jitter, whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. Make one change, ported from E044 (drafts/E044_res3_submission.py): 24 px for epochs 0-1.5 as now, then 28 px whole images (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip, translate and jitter) for epochs 1.5-3.0, then 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs. Total epochs, bs and every step-indexed schedule stay unchanged, so the sample stream and lr values are identical to E045. A switch that falls mid-epoch uses the first part of that epoch's permutation at the old resolution and the rest at the new one. The 28 px graph's final pool is F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to its final map (expect 3x3). Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (E009). In build(), warm up the 28 px train step without whitening-bias grad at bs 1536, plus every partial-batch shape at both switches, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Check that total build time stays under ~450 s (E044 took 232 s for 6 variants). If I060's 20 px first stage was kept first, apply this change to that commit instead and leave its first stage alone. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.

Follow up E045 on the head lr axis. RMS-matched test of scheduled orthogonalization strength. This is the form requested when I054 was dropped, so that a result is not confounded with a lower effective Muon lr (H1.2.4). On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change inside the batched compiled Muon step. Today each momentum matrix is scaled to Frobenius norm 1 before NS3. Run the same 3 quintic iterations, then rescale each NS output matrix so its Frobenius norm equals that of the tip's NS output for that shape group (or, more simply, sqrt(min(out,in)) times the existing sqrt(max(1,out/in)) factor). The per-step update magnitude is therefore unchanged, and only how strongly the small singular directions are flattened changes. In drafts/, log the per-group update Frobenius norm and the fraction of singular values above 0.5 at steps 0, 100 and the end, against the tip, to confirm the norms match and the spectrum is less whitened late in training.
